documentation_policy.reason: Repository CI intentionally rejects tracked Markdown; this machine-readable artifact is the tracked Phase 8D status, evidence index, claim-boundary record, and verification handoff.

core_web_vitals_lab.scope: The LCP and CLS lab regression ceilings align with the published good Core Web Vitals thresholds. The 200 ms value is used only as a scripted lab interaction ceiling; this repository does not describe Event Timing samples as field INP.

deterministic_compute.scope: These are repository-enforced deterministic local-compute regression ceilings from the certified Phase 8D performance checkpoint, not network or end-user latency SLAs.

api_in_process.scope: The selected ASGI measurements are reporting-only in-process baselines. They exclude network, reverse-proxy, deployment, and real-user latency; no API latency pass threshold is frozen.

representative_hardware_wwt.scope: The operator tool records WWT WebGL draw-bearing animation-frame cadence. It is not GPU-completion timing and no project cadence floor is frozen; an optional operator floor must be supplied explicitly.

manual_evidence_required.reason: Automated axe, landmarks, focus, contrast, touch, and fallback checks do not prove full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. A strict completeness validator is available, but no manually collected WCAG review artifact exists yet.

ARIA roles and automated accessibility-tree checks are not equivalent to testing with a real screen reader. A strict completeness validator is available, but no manually collected real-screen-reader artifact exists yet.

Headed Chromium now has supporting automation using the browser's native default page-zoom setting at exactly 200%, with eight representative routes sampled without document-level horizontal overflow. docs/16_TESTING_QUALITY.md still explicitly requires the 200% zoom check in the manual accessibility set, so human review remains pending.

CPU/network emulation is a synthetic proxy and does not replace representative low-end hardware testing. A strict completeness validator is available, but no observation from an actual low-end device exists yet.

Headed Chromium used a positively identified hardware renderer with real WWT network access. The recorded draw-bearing frame cadence is representative-hardware evidence, not GPU-completion timing or a pass without an explicit floor.

manual_evidence_required.reason: A strict privacy-bounded importer now validates externally collected aggregate field-INP evidence without adding behavioral tracking to Lumina. No approved deployed field export has been imported, so scripted Event Timing remains lab evidence and the field-INP requirement is still pending.

Representative headed Chromium profiling used Linux i915 DRM fdinfo across five client-side WWT activate/leave cycles with DRM clients preserved independently and the WebGL renderer bound through Chromium's render node to the sampled PCI device. The generated evidence records each client's post-leave resident-memory series plus first, final, and maximum observations so cycle-to-cycle changes remain visible. DRM fdinfo cannot attribute those allocations specifically to Lumina or WWT and no project memory floor is frozen, so the recorded result remains observational rather than a performance pass, a leak diagnosis, or proof of full cleanup.

claim_boundaries: CSS or viewport reflow proxies are not described as real browser zoom evidence.
Native Chromium 200% browser-zoom automation is not described as completion of the required manual 200% zoom accessibility check.
Automated axe results are not described as screen-reader or WCAG certification.
A manual-evidence validator is not described as a performed human accessibility or representative-device observation.
A generated manual-review worksheet or template is not described as manual evidence, a performed observation, or Phase 8D completion.
Manual reduced-motion and canvas-alternative observations are admissible only when their recorded environments explicitly confirm reduced-motion mode and WebGL-disabled mode respectively.

An unavailable manual observation may record that its required specialized environment or device capability was unavailable; inconclusive and observed statuses still require that capability to be present and recorded.
A manual evidence artifact cannot summarize itself as inconclusive or unavailable when any required observation records an observed finding.
Operator-supplied manual and field-INP JSON evidence inputs are accepted only as bounded regular files; final-component symlinks and non-regular files are rejected before parsing.
Manual evidence, manual protocol strings, and field-INP evidence or approval text reject non-printable control/format characters while retaining visible international Unicode.

Every tracked field-INP approval-manifest trust record and approved export is validated independently for admissible metadata, referential integrity, ordered observation windows, INP metric identity, and coherent sample/value pairs before evidence import.

Protocol v1 status semantics, journey/check uniqueness, manual-journey references, and null generic pass thresholds are fail-closed across manual validation, worksheet generation, and field-INP import; semantic expansion requires an explicit protocol/code version change.

Field-INP approval timestamps and approved export windows may not be future-dated, and recorded browser-zoom, representative-WWT, and GPU-memory observation timestamps must be timezone-aware ISO-8601 values that are not in the future.
Scripted lab interaction latency is not described as field INP.
A field-INP evidence validator or empty import path is not described as field INP evidence.
Phase 8D field-INP readiness does not add behavioral tracking to Lumina; only approved aggregate external evidence may be imported.
Synthetic CPU/network throttling is not described as representative low-end hardware evidence.
In-process ASGI latency is not described as deployed HTTP, proxy, network, or real-user latency.
WWT draw-bearing animation-frame cadence is not described as GPU-complete frame timing, and representative-hardware eligibility is not described as a performance pass without an explicit floor.
Representative DRM memory observations are not described as whole-engine GPU disposal, zero retention, or a universal GPU-memory pass threshold.
